the_one_question: Does `bash /runpod-volume/start.sh` execute as the worker's main process, and if yes, where does it stop before its first print?
the_answer: It executes, and it does not stop. The wrapped start command produced a 20,827-byte log on the volume showing the RunPod SDK's serverless job loop booting, passing its seven fitness checks, taking the queued job, loading 1,188 weight shards and finishing. The job returned COMPLETED with the full `info` payload. The serverless job-loop branch of scripts/start_5b_worker.sh -- which had never executed in this project before today -- works end to end on the staged volume.

what_this_did_not_establish.why_srv2b_hung: Two things differ between srv-2b and srv-2c, not one: the wrapper AND a day of platform time. The console would not render for either side that evening, which is itself evidence of a log-plane incident -- and that is exactly the condition under which an unbuffered write to an undrained stdout pipe blocks forever. Nothing in hand separates 'the redirect fixed it' from 'the platform was broken on 08-08'.
what_this_did_not_establish.the_measurement_that_would: one endpoint with the UNWRAPPED `bash,/runpod-volume/start.sh`, one job. Today's reading prices it at about $0.06. It is NOT bought here: step 4 forbids fixes beyond the guard, and the briefing is the operator's.
what_this_did_not_establish.parity_3_11_2: untouched. No row of test v4 was opened, no head has a verdict, and the single attempt SPEC 3.11 (2) grants is still unspent.

ranked_hypotheses_for_srv2b.hypothesis: a transient platform fault in EU-RO-1's serverless plane on 08-08
ranked_hypotheses_for_srv2b.fits: everything srv-2b saw, and the fact that nothing was changed on the volume
ranked_hypotheses_for_srv2b.against: the mock-worker control completed on the same class the same evening
ranked_hypotheses_for_srv2b.testable_for: the same $0.06 -- the two hypotheses share one experiment
ranked_hypotheses_for_srv2b.verdict_after_the_control: PROMOTED to rank 1. Two runs twenty minutes apart, one wrapped and one not, both answered on the same volume, datacenter and class. What changed since srv-2b is the platform, not our start command.

ranked_hypotheses_for_srv2b.hypothesis: a blocked write to an undrained stdout pipe. start.sh execs `python -u`, so every print goes straight to fd 1; if RunPod's log collector stopped draining the container's pipe, the first write past the 64 KB buffer blocks forever.
ranked_hypotheses_for_srv2b.fits: zero console lines at any level; a worker 'running' with a job it never took; the console not rendering for either side; and a redirect to a file curing it.
ranked_hypotheses_for_srv2b.against: the vendor mock-worker on the same volume/DC/class completed that evening -- though it prints far less and its job took 144 ms.
ranked_hypotheses_for_srv2b.verdict_after_the_control: DEMOTED. The unwrapped command COMPLETED, so a blocked stdout write is not a standing property of running our container without the redirect. It could still describe what happened on 08-08 if the log plane was degraded THEN, but it is no longer the hypothesis the evidence points at.

ranked_hypotheses_for_srv2b.hypothesis: the start command is not what the worker runs under the stock image
ranked_hypotheses_for_srv2b.why: the image declares Entrypoint /opt/nvidia/nvidia_entrypoint.sh with CMD /start.sh; --docker-start-cmd replaces the CMD and the entrypoint execs it. The boot log exists and is the SDK's own output, so the command ran.

observations_worth_a_runbook_line.a_worker_is_ready_before_the_first_job: health read {idle:1, ready:1} seconds after `serverless create` and before any job was submitted. The runbook's 'creation is free; workers bill only on a request' is not what the platform does -- something boots at creation.
observations_worth_a_runbook_line.no_log_channel_outside_the_console: runpodctl has no `logs` verb for serverless, and rest.runpod.io returns 400 on /endpoints/{id}/workers, /endpoints/{id}/logs and /workers?endpointId=. Worker output is console-only, which is why redirecting it to the volume is the only durable channel this project has.
observations_worth_a_runbook_line.fitness_checks_are_free_diagnostics: the SDK runs seven of them before the first job -- GPU binary, memory, disk, network, CUDA version, CUDA init, matmul benchmark -- and prints the results. They took 3,993.55 ms and every one passed.

unwrapped_control.why: The operator authorised it on the srv-2c report at ~$0.06. srv-2c answered its own question but could not say why srv-2b hung, because two things differed: the wrapper and a day of platform time. This holds the platform fixed -- same evening, same volume, same datacenter, same class, twenty minutes apart -- and moves only the start command back to srv-2b's.
unwrapped_control.verdict: The unwrapped command -- srv-2b's exact argv ['bash','/runpod-volume/start.sh'] -- was picked up and answered. The wrapper was NOT what fixed srv-2c, so the wrapper was not what broke srv-2b. Pre-registered reading: srv-2b's hang was the platform on the evening of 08-08, not our container and not our start command.
unwrapped_control.why_300_not_600: a hang pays for the observation window, not for work. The wrapped job was picked up in 15.9 s and finished at 174 s, so 300 s is a generous margin that caps the downside near $0.10 instead of $0.18.

the_execution_time_gap.observation: the unwrapped run took 34% longer to execute. Directionally consistent with stdout costing something -- the weight loader writes ~1,188 tqdm updates, to a file when wrapped and to the container's log pipe when not -- but it is n=1 against n=1 on different workers, so it is an observation and not a finding. It would take a handful of paired runs to become one.
